Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, then use the required wake-visual and fish-control skills to inspect the inherited evidence before touching the solver. I’ll keep the candidate and the two required documentation updates tightly scoped to this Phase 2 workspace.

The workspace requires a visual-first comparison and explicitly forbids local CFD. I’m now anchoring the four sampled candidates to their scores, observations, metrics, diagnostics, and inherited guidance; after that I’ll inspect the combined wake sheets and only then choose one compact controller mechanism.

All four samples satisfy the direct uniform still-water contract and all capture, so there is no sampled semantic failure. I’ll use the best-score rollout and the slowest/worst-score capture as the strongest contrast, treating the latter as a performance regression rather than inventing a failure class. The visual skill is now driving the next action: inspect both top-down vorticity and oblique Lambda2 rows in each combined sheet.

The sampled response-gated posterior bend is the best of the four (`19.360T`, distance integral `2.08911L`, score `-0.19989`), while the other actuator-shape variants remain within a narrow capture envelope. Since the inherited bank documents repeated capture-class iterations without a semantic change—and warns against more terminal gates or scalar tuning—I’m consulting the fish-control shelf for a genuinely distinct, state-feedback mechanism. Any adopted idea will be translated only as a normalized body-frame invariant.

The strongest actionable signal is not a route defect: the two visual sheets show nearly identical coherent alternating wakes, self-propelled target approach, and a smooth terminal hook. The differentiator is actuator use: every sample reaches the exact `260°/T` joint-rate ceiling, and the best sample spends about `37.1%/33.3%` of steps above 90% of the smooth acceleration bound. I’m selecting a small actuator-aware rate governor: it will attenuate only acceleration that pushes an already-near-limit joint farther into saturation, while leaving braking and the proven target/capture scaffold intact. This is a new feedback mechanism, not gain-only tuning.

The inherited optimizer logs sharpen the boundary: a previous-command effort gate produced only a trivial headroom change and worsened arrival, so I will not repeat command-history gating. The candidate will instead restore the clean symmetric posterior-lag scaffold and test one distinct posterior-path mechanism based on normalized measured tail-joint rate. It should materially cut wasted same-direction acceleration at the hard rate ceiling while preserving braking, anterior steering, wake phase lag, and terminal redirect. I’m recording that diagnosis and falsification criteria now, before editing the policy as required by the visual skill.

The candidate now differs by one mechanism only: the unproven wrong-sign-yaw curvature residual is removed, and the posterior rate governor is added to the proven lag scaffold. I’m now distilling the reusable lesson into the inherited experience bank without claiming this unevaluated candidate as evidence; the lesson will separate what the sampled CFD establishes from what the next rollout must falsify.

The documentation contract is complete. Per the workspace instructions, I’m invoking the dedicated non-CFD check runner now; it will verify the semantic guidance delta, Julia policy contract/schema, and editable-file boundary.

The manual delta is clean: the only solver change is the candidate policy, and the durable lesson is a substantive replacement tied to sampled metrics and inherited negative evidence. While the formal checker runs, I’m adding one lightweight synthetic boundary sweep (no CFD) to exercise both signs of the new rate-governor branch, since the standard contract fixture uses zero joint rate.

The checker found one workspace-metadata defect and one environment limitation: the rendered README lists the same prefill guidance example twice, so the semantic checker cannot identify a unique parent; Julia is also absent from `PATH`. The solver boundary already passes. I’ll remove only the duplicate parent marker, rerun the semantic check, and locate any workspace/host Julia binary before deciding whether the runtime check can be completed.

The semantic check now passes after removing only the duplicated prefill listing. A host Julia binary exists at `julia`; I’m rerunning the dedicated checker with that directory prepended to `PATH`, including all three checks from scratch as required.

A trace-level cross-check confirms the governor is neither dormant nor global: the posterior rate lies above 80% of its ceiling for about `21.8–22.1%` of samples, but acceleration is pushing farther into that band for only `9.7–10.3%`. That supports the chosen branch semantics—selective unloading, with braking untouched—and I’m adding this calibration to the evidence record.

The dedicated checker has passed all three checks. I made one evidence-only refinement to the notes and durable lesson after that pass, so I’m doing a final semantic and boundary recheck; the already-passing candidate code itself is unchanged.

Implemented exactly one candidate: [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1).

- Adds selective posterior joint-rate anti-windup while preserving braking and the capture scaffold.
- Records visual diagnosis, bookshelf transfer, and falsification criteria in [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1).
- Materially revises the reusable evidence lesson in [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:56).
- Removed a duplicated prefill entry from `README.md` that prevented parent-guidance validation.

All required checks pass: semantic guidance delta, Julia policy contract/schema, finite boundary sweep, and solver edit boundary. No CFD was run.
